clue.text: Fine report outlining origin of alternative facts circulating about Italy

indicators.note: to outline something is to draw round its edge, so one piece wraps around the rest
about here means around, so the mixed letters go round the next piece

parts.note: a report in a newspaper is a story

indicators.note: things circulating move about and change places, so these letters get mixed up
the origin of a word is where it starts, so only its opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word
taken as written, to be rearranged
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A sly dig at a news report that spins 'alternative facts' about Italy, yet calls it fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' sits at the front like a verdict on the report, but it is the definition. I is the international vehicle code for Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory means acceptable or good enough, the same everyday sense as saying something is fine.

clue.text: Puts out peel of sizable fruit

indicators.note: a peel is the outer skin, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
dates are a fruit of the palm tree

explanation.surface: Someone throws away the skin of a big piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts out' looks like discarding the peel, but it means knocks someone out with a drug. 'Peel' sits well with fruit while working as the outer-letters signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To sedate a patient is to render them unconscious or drowsy with drugs, one sense of putting someone out.

clue.text: Clan accepting promotion for gay woman

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a clan is a tribe
an ad, or advertisement, promotes a product

explanation.surface: A family group agrees to promote one of its members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promotion' suggests a step up in rank, but here it is advertising, abbreviated AD as usual in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribade is a dated, literary term for a lesbian, so it names a gay woman.

clue.text: Small tee between posts damaged part of golf club?

indicators.note: to sit between things is to be enclosed by them, so one piece goes inside the other
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters lose their order

parts.note: the letter whose name is spelt tee
taken as written, to be rearranged
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A golfer finds a little tee lodged between broken posts and wonders what bit of the club is hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tee' looks like golf equipment but is simply the letter T. WEET sits after the first S of SSPOT, a rearrangement of POSTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet spot is the area on a clubface that strikes the ball most effectively; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: Language in ship seeking the Golden Fleece for Troy

parts.note: the Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts in search of the Golden Fleece
t is the abbreviation for troy, the weight system used for precious metals

explanation.surface: A Greek legend: the language spoken aboard Jason's ship as it headed for Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Troy suggests the city of Greek legend, fitting the Argonauts, but it is troy weight, abbreviated t.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the slang or jargon of a particular group, a specialised form of language.

clue.text: Rushed round island in support for apprentice

indicators.note: to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it, so this group goes into the next piece

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, to rush
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone dashes round an island to bring help to a young apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' is the small peg that holds up a golf ball, not help or backing; two insertions nest one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone learning a trade on the job, just like an apprentice.

clue.text: Artist attached to her work left in charge of transport

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: something that has left is no longer there, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: the artist's work is a painting or picture
IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge
simply joins the two pieces side by side

explanation.surface: An artist devoted to her work is left running the transport department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Her' refers back to the artist, so her work is a PICTURE; IC leaves it to give PTURE. 'Transport' is not vehicles but an overwhelming emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport can mean a state of intense joy or ecstasy, as in transports of delight, which is rapture.

clue.text: Teacher rearranged the classroom

indicators.note: rearranging things puts them in a new order, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher moves the desks around in the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of THE CLASSROOM make SCHOOLMASTER exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is a male teacher in a school, a slightly old-fashioned term for the job.

clue.text: Drug company badly need to contain source of inflammation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: to contain is to hold within, so one piece wraps round another
done badly means done wrong, so these letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A drug firm urgently needs something to bring inflammation under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug company' reads as a single phrase, but the definition is just 'Drug'; company is CO. DENE, a jumble of NEED, holds the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is an opiate painkiller derived from morphine, so it is a drug.

clue.text: Aquatic animal showing mass discharge

parts.note: a gram is a unit of mass
pus is a discharge from an infected wound

explanation.surface: A sea creature puts on a display of releasing a great deal of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass discharge' looks like a single large outpouring, but it is two separate pieces, a unit of mass and a bodily discharge.
explanation.definitionFit: Grampus is the name for Risso's dolphin, and was formerly used for the killer whale, both creatures of the sea.

clue.text: Animal planned to explode in fairground attraction

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it, so the scattered letters sit within the next piece

parts.note: a coconut shy is a fairground stall where people throw balls at coconuts

indicators.note: exploding blows something apart, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal was meant to blow up at a funfair ride, a sinister scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planned to explode' reads as a bomb plot, but 'planned to' is the material to jumble. A shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shetland pony is a small, sturdy breed of horse from the Scottish islands, so an animal.

clue.text: Exhausted actors in exile

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for a noun or adjective answer: an outcast is someone cast out

parts.note: out can mean used up or exhausted, as supplies run out
the cast of a play is its actors

explanation.surface: A troupe of worn-out performers have been banished abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' suggests tired, but here it means used up, as in run out.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is someone rejected and driven away from society, so living as if banished from home.

clue.text: Hairstyle in sport coming back in various tones

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the letters run backwards
placed in something means put inside it, so this goes within the other piece
various suggests different arrangements, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A particular haircut returns to fashion in sport, available in a range of shades.
explanation.walkthrough: RU for rugby union is a standard crossword abbreviation for sport; turned round it sits inside TONSE, a reordering of TONES.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonsure is the shaved crown worn by monks, which is a particular way of cutting the hair.

clue.text: Rejected measure of cloth containing silicon material

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters run the other way
containing means holding inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an ell is an old unit for measuring cloth, about 45 inches
Si is the chemical symbol for silicon

explanation.surface: A length of fabric with silicon in it has been turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure of cloth' tempts one toward 'material' as fabric, but an ell is an old unit of length; the whole insertion is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread or fabric, often used for stockings, so a type of material.

clue.text: Gradually, quiet announced before supper, say

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we want a word that sounds like the clue word

parts.note: peace means quiet, and it is said the same way as piece
supper is an example of a meal, as 'say' signals

explanation.surface: A call for silence is made just before the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks supper as an example of the wider category.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something piecemeal means doing it bit by bit, in stages, rather than all at once.

clue.text: English plant, say, given to German as a seasonal gift

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower
eg, for example, is what 'say' means here
G is the abbreviation for German, added on the end

explanation.surface: An English gardener hands a German friend a plant as a holiday present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like it marks plant as an example, but it gives its own piece, EG.
explanation.definitionFit: An Easter egg is a chocolate egg given as a present at Easter, so a gift tied to a time of year.

clue.text: Equipment suitable to welcome soldier to America

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: apt means suitable
a para is a paratrooper
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Gear fit for greeting a serviceman arriving in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'to' belongs to the insertion signal, the second simply adds US on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is the technical equipment or machinery needed for a particular job.

clue.text: Squad extremely grabbed by suggestion

indicators.note: something grabbed is held tightly, so it ends up inside the holder

parts.note: a plan is a proposal or suggestion
too means excessively, extremely

explanation.surface: A team is seized upon by a proposal with great enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an adverb modifying 'grabbed', but it supplies its own small word.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small unit of soldiers, a military squad commanded by a lieutenant.

clue.text: Cloth fastener covering large contemptible person

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery

indicators.note: a covering goes around what it hides, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a tie fastens things together
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A clasp on some fabric hides a big, nasty character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cloth fastener' reads as one item, a button perhaps, but it splits into a fabric and a separate fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a reptile is an insult for a sly, cold, despicable individual, likening them to a snake.

clue.text: Setter eating shell of exotic nut

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside, so one piece is swallowed by another

parts.note: Pan is the name of this puzzle's setter

indicators.note: a shell is the outer casing, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler cracks open and eats a foreign nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' usually means the compiler, often ME or I; here it is the pseudonym Pan, whose name is on this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pecan is the edible nut of a hickory tree from North America, often used in pies.

clue.text: Almost wander into office of cathedral official

indicators.note: going into something means ending up inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a post is a job or office

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to rove is to wander

explanation.surface: Someone nearly strays into the workplace of a church dignitary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' suggests a room, but it is a position, as in holding office.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Church of England a provost is the head of the chapter at certain cathedrals, a senior clergyman.

clue.text: Jeweller's nurse carrying note

definitions.note: the definition is possessive; read as 'Jeweller is' it names the firm

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a carer looks after the sick, as a nurse does
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A nurse at a jewellery shop is holding a message.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Jeweller's' reads as 'is', so the clue says the jeweller is a nurse carrying a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartier is the famous French luxury firm of jewellers and watchmakers, founded in Paris.

clue.text: Caught priests involved in illegitimate trade

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so one piece sits within another
something illegitimate is not proper, so these letters are put out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
P is short for priest, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Clergymen are arrested for their part in black-market dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: P for priest is a standard abbreviation, so doubling it makes the plural, much as pp stands for pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapped means captured or snared with no means of escape, which is to be caught.

clue.text: Poke Italian's toe

parts.note: a dig is a poke, as in the ribs
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: An instruction to jab an Italian person's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's looks possessive but means 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Digit is the anatomical word for any finger or toe, so a toe is one example.

clue.text: Eastern stagehand covering books in exercise in self-aggrandisement

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for Eastern

indicators.note: a covering goes around what it hides, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a grip is a stagehand who moves scenery
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A theatre worker from the East wraps books while showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: A grip is the theatre or film worker who shifts scenery; OT for the Old Testament books is a standard crossword shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done chiefly to boost one's own sense of importance, which is self-aggrandisement.

clue.text: Outfit worn by suspect into disturbing the peace

indicators.note: clothes worn by someone go around them, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a rig is a set of clothes, a rig-out

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious or not right, so these letters are out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A suspect wearing a particular outfit is keen on causing a public disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a noun for a person under suspicion, and 'into' like 'keen on'; both serve the anagram instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioting is violent public disorder by a crowd, the most serious kind of breach of the peace.

clue.text: Feeling generated by Ireland's third poet laureate

indicators.note: third points to the letter in position three of the word

parts.note: the third letter of the word
Andrew Motion was the UK Poet Laureate from 1999 to 2009

explanation.surface: Strong sentiment stirred up by a celebrated poet from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ireland's third poet laureate' looks like the third holder of an Irish title, but it is a single letter followed by the English laureate Andrew Motion.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a strong mental state such as joy or anger, so a feeling in the ordinary sense.

clue.text: Detective with unsteady gait held by one with money to place

indicators.note: something held by another sits within its grasp, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an investor places money in ventures

indicators.note: something unsteady wobbles out of position, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wobbly-walking sleuth is being bankrolled by a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: The long phrase at the end defines a person who puts money into ventures; the jumbled walk is tucked into the middle of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: An investigator is someone who looks into crimes or matters officially or privately, a detective.
